newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total says signed crude deal with Iraq. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Total says signed crude deal with Iraq. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]

text.p: French oil group Total SA said on Monday that it had signed a contract with Iraq to take 30,000 barrels of oil per day, provided the United Nations approves the agreement.

"We have reached an agreement with the Iraqis (corrects from Iranians) at the end of last week to take 30,000 barrels per day. We now await approval by the United Nations," a spokesman for Total said.
At Elf Aquitaine there was no immediate reaction on whether the company has also signed a contract.
Mitsubishi Corp of Japan was the first company on Monday to say it had signed a deal of Friday, in their case for 40,000 barrels per day.
The United Nations allows Iraq to sell $2.0 billion in crude over six months to pay for food and medicine.
U.N. overseers have so far approved five contracts. U.S. firms coastal Corp and Bay Oil on Sunday began lifting crude oil from the southern export outlet of Mina a-Bakr.
Other firms having been granted U.N. approval included Turkish state oil company TUPRAS and Italy's Oil Energy.
